body_ar:
لله تعالى صفات مذكورة في الكتاب والسنة، وقد خالف في إثباتها المشبهة والمعطلة، وقد ذكر أهل السنة قواعد ترد على الفرقتين، وتبين الطريقة السليمة في إثبات صفات الله الذاتية والفعلية من غير انحراف.
الكلام على قاعدة (القول في صفات الله كالقول في ذاته ونفسه)
يقول الشيخ حفظه الله: [وما نقول في صفات قدسه فرع الذي نقوله في نفس....]
الرد بالقاعدة على المشبهة والمعطلة:
هذا شروع في وضع قواعد لتوحيد الأسماء والصفات، وهذه القواعد أهمها قاعدتان: أولاهما: أن القول في الصفات كالقول في الذات، وهذه القاعدة هي التي نظمها في هذا البيت بقوله: (وما نقول في صفات قدسه فرع الذي نقوله في نفسه) أي: إن الكلام في صفاته مثل الكلام في ذاته، وهذه مزيلة لكل إشكال، سواء كان من جهة المعطلة أو من جهة المشبهة: أما من جهة المعطلة: فإنهم يثبتون له نفساً هي الذات عندهم، وهم يعرفون أن للمخلوق ذاتاً ومع ذلك لا يقتضي إثبات أن له ذاتاً وأن للمخلوق ذاتاً التشبيه قطعاً عندهم! فما الفرق بينها وبين الوجه واليدين والعين والقدم والساق؟!...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* God, exalted is He, has attributes mentioned in the Book and the Sunnah. The anthropomorphists (al-Mushabbihah) and those who divest God of His attributes (al-Muʿaṭṭilah) have dissented over affirming them, and the People of the Sunnah have set out rules that answer both groups and that show the sound way of affirming God's essential and active attributes without deviation.

## On the rule that what is said of God's attributes is what is said of His essence and His self

The Sheikh, may God preserve him, says:

*[And what we say concerning the attributes of His holiness is derivative of what we say concerning His self ……]*

## Answering the anthropomorphists and those who divest God of His attributes by means of this rule

This begins the laying down of rules for the oneness of the names and attributes. The most important of these rules are two. The first is that what is said of the attributes is what is said of the essence, and this is the rule he set in verse in this line, in his words: "And what we say concerning the attributes of His holiness is derivative of what we say concerning His self." That is to say: speech about His attributes is like speech about His essence. This removes every difficulty, whether it comes from the side of those who divest God of His attributes or from the side of the anthropomorphists.

As for the side of those who divest Him of His attributes: they do affirm that He has a self, which in their view is the essence; and they know that the created thing has an essence too; and even so, in their view, affirming that He has an essence and that the created thing has an essence does not entail likening Him to creation — definitively not, on their own account. What, then, is the difference between the essence and the face, the two hands, the eye, the foot and the shin?!…

translator_notes: One of a run of fourteen records, IDs 734-747, the series 'The Names and Attributes', all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/esmawesivat-* series, numbered 1 to 14 in the same order as the IDs.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

This record does carry a CMS timestamp in a .create_date span (10 May 2011, within a 28-minute window shared by the whole run 738-747). That is a bulk-upload timestamp for the series, not the date the lesson was given, and it is not evidence of composition date. Record 737, translated in an earlier wave, reports no date for this run; the timestamp is in fact present in the page and should be backfilled there.
Creedal material. Per style guide section 8, the vocabulary of divine attributes is not the vocabulary of the five legal rulings and the five-rulings mapping is not applied anywhere in this record.

The record breaks off in the middle of the answer to the first group. The second of the two rules is announced and never stated, and the answer to the anthropomorphists is never given at all. Marked critical_for_display: a reader will otherwise take a rhetorical question put to one opponent for the whole of the Sheikh's teaching on the point.

The quoted line is from the versified base text the lesson expounds, and the source itself truncates it mid-word ('في نفس....'). The English completes the word from the prose restatement that follows two lines later in the same record, and marks nothing else.
